After approval, runExecProcess can acquire that old identity and launch the command without rereading the session store. findings.body: When workspace and cwd are the same subdirectory of a repository, this early return skips resolving the repository top level. readTaskCompletionCandidate runs prefix-limited ls-files there, so source identifies the repository HEAD while input and dirty hashes omit tracked siblings. findings.body: A populated gitlink directory without a .git entry is hashed as the constant uninitialized-gitlink. Git does not enumerate indexed gitlink contents as ordinary untracked files, so subsequent edits to consumed module code can leave both candidate digests unchanged and preserve stale completion evidence. Classify gitlinks by index mode and bind their physical source, or reject unresolved populated gitlinks; the async reader has the same omissions.

findings.title: Workspace Git config can execute a helper during task candidate readback
findings.body: The new `readTaskCompletionCandidate` runs `git diff --cached --binary HEAD` and `git diff --binary` against the active workspace without `--no-ext-diff` or a cleared `diff.external`. A workspace-local Git config can set `diff.external` (and related helper settings), so opening an untrusted project and triggering completion snapshot/admission can launch a repository-selected program. Treat the workspace as untrusted: pass `--no-ext-diff`, disable local fsmonitor/diff drivers, or use a bounded Git plumbing path that cannot execute configured helpers.

findings.title: Final completion commit trusts pre-lock config and task-loop owner records
findings.body: `validateCurrentOwner` rereads the candidate with `refs.currentCandidate.configSha256`, which is the digest captured before the journal ticket, rather than the current runtime config. For `task-loop-exec-effect` it also uses the prior `check` object instead of rereading the TaskLoop checkpoint, effect receipt, and archive. A hot reload or stale checkpoint/effect replacement between `readReferences` and append therefore passes the final check and commits an acceptance for owner data that is no longer current. Reread the current config and TaskLoop evidence at the final boundary, or bind the operation to a current CAS revision that the final writer rechecks.

findings.title: Sandbox-owned verification processes are rejected by the TaskLoop verifier
findings.body: `runTaskLoopVerificationCheck` passes `resolveSandboxContext` into `createOpenClawCodingTools`, but when a sandbox is active `runExecProcess` sets `lifecycleOwner: "sandbox"`. The guard only accepts `native` and `verseshell`, so every sandboxed TaskLoop verification returns `unavailable` without a receipt. This disables the sandbox path the task contract explicitly requires. Accept the host-owned sandbox lifecycle while retaining the pid/exited/output checks, or route verification through another supported local owner.

findings.title: Append route can create a model-authored done business task without a claim
findings.body: `projectTaskLedgerSnapshot` applies the automatic-completion guard only when `node.owner === 'agent'` or a prior automatic marker exists. The public `appendEvents` route accepts a caller-supplied `node_created` event with `kind: 'task'`, `status: 'done'`, and no `owner` (or `owner: 'user'`) while `actor` is `'assistant'`; the projection then leaves the node done and adds no `automaticCompletion` marker. Thus a caller can bypass the completion-claim path without ever producing a `completionDecision`. The raw append path must reject or normalize every non-user business terminal event, independent of the optional owner field.

findings.title: Caller-selected taskLedgerRootId can overwrite an existing manual task
findings.body: `ensureLongTaskLedgerRoot` marks every `source: 'task_loop'` root as `automaticCompletion` pending, while `runTaskLoop` passes the model/tool-supplied `request.taskLedgerRootId` directly through. `appendLongTaskLedgerEvents` writes a new `node_created` event for that id without checking whether the node already exists, so a caller can name an existing manual task and have its title, status, and metadata replaced by a TaskLoop root that is now eligible for automatic completion. Validate that the supplied root is a TaskLoop-owned node or allocate a fresh id; do not convert an existing manual node.

findings.title: Rejected completion decisions overwrite manual or previously accepted done
findings.body: The `completion_decided` projection always sets `status` to `done` when accepted and `review` when rejected. A rejected claim with a missing or invalid checkpoint therefore downgrades an automatic task that was manually set done or that already had a valid accepted decision; repeated failed attempts can keep changing the task. Preserve the existing manual or accepted state unless this is the current pending acceptance, or record a rejected claim as a separate pending/readback fact that cannot overwrite a completed state.

findings.title: Replay returns a superseded accepted decision instead of current state
findings.body: The replay branch returns the historical `decision` attached to the requested operation without comparing it with the node's current `completionDecision` or readback. After a later rejected or superseded decision, replaying an older accepted operation can return `decision.accepted: true` while the returned snapshot is `review` (or belongs to a different accepted decision). A caller using the result contract can therefore treat a stale acceptance as current. Return the current decision/readback for the claim, or mark historical replay explicitly and keep it separate from the current decision field.

findings.title: Invalidated completion readback is bypassed by chat, session, and export reads
findings.body: `readCurrentTaskLedgerCompletions` is only applied by the `createTaskLedgerApi` routes. `chat-api.applyTaskLedgerContext`, the `sessions-api` task summary, and `exportHtml` call `loadTaskLedgerSnapshot` directly, so after source/config/checkpoint or acceptance drift they continue to expose the persisted `done` status. The model context, session summary, and exported HTML can therefore still show a stale successful task even though the host API reports it invalidated. Route these consumers through the same completion readback/invalidation path or invalidate at the snapshot load boundary.

reviewR21.overall_explanation: The patch contains substantial A3 plumbing, but it does not satisfy the original six requirements and five acceptance criteria. The final admission boundary is a TOCTOU path for config and TaskLoop checkpoint/effect changes; sandbox execution is rejected; raw append and caller-selected root paths can produce business done outside claim admission; rejected and replay paths can impose or present stale state; and invalidated readback is only applied on one host API route. The supplied evidence is explicitly development-only, not a clean actual positive/negative acceptance chain, so these are blockers to A3 acceptance rather than merely unit-test gaps.

findings.title: Completed TaskLoop runs no longer record progress 100 on the goal/task nodes
findings.body: `recordTaskLoopLedgerLifecycle` now derives `status` from `projectTaskLoopTaskStatus(event.status)` (complete → `review`), but the two terminal progress events still compute the default with `event.progress ?? (status === 'done' || status === 'blocked' ? 100 : undefined)` (lines 347 for the goal node and 369 for the task node). A finished loop now projects to `review`, so with no explicit `event.progress` the payload carries `progress: undefined`; `projectTaskLedgerSnapshot`'s `progress_changed` case then overwrites the node with `clampProgress(undefined)` → `undefined`, erasing any previously reported progress instead of recording 100 as before. The mission path (line 566, `missionLedgerStatus`) and clawgraph path (line 693) still map completion to `done` and keep 100, so this is a task-loop-only silent behavior change with no test covering it. Fix by keying the progress default off the runtime fact (e.g. `event.status === 'complete'`) or treating `review` as terminal for progress.

findings.title: verseshell-host-receipt completion branch reads an evidence root no producer writes
findings.body: `taskLedgerVerificationEvidenceRoot` (electron/services/task-ledger-completion.ts:21) points the completion reader at `<task-ledger-dir>/verification-evidence`, and `readReferences` uses `readCompletedVerseGitTaskCheck(runId, ...)` (line 47; again at line 145) as the primary source for `owner: 'verseshell-host-receipt'` checks. A repo-wide search shows `FileVerseShellReceiptAuthority` is only constructed inside that helper plus tests, and `prepareCandidateVerificationEvidence` (the only caller of `recordPlan`/`recordAuthorization`/`recordReceipt`, i.e. the only writer) has no production caller. Consequently nothing in production ever populates that root, so the verseshell check path can never be admitted and only the Gateway-supplied `task-loop-exec-effect` receipts can satisfy completion; the verseshell behavior is exercised solely by synthetic fixtures that use a test-owned root. Either wire the host receipt writer to this root, or remove/annotate the dead branch so the code does not imply an end-to-end host-receipt path that does not exist yet.

findings.title: Full tracked-tree Git candidate scan runs on Main polling/hot paths with no cross-snapshot reuse
findings.body: `readCurrentTaskLedgerCompletions` re-derives every accepted completion by calling `readReferences`, which calls `readTaskCompletionCandidateAsync` (line 42). That reader spawns three `git` processes (`rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `ls-files --others`, `ls-files --stage`) and then reads and SHA-256s the bytes of every tracked file plus every tracked mode. The candidate map is deliberately per-snapshot only, so this cost recurs on every call. It is now reached from `sessionActivity.snapshot` (electron/services/session-activity-api.ts:123/138, a UI polling path), from `chat` message handling (electron/services/chat-api.ts:157/270) and from session summaries (electron/services/sessions-api.ts:2683). For any workspace that has at least one accepted completion, each poll/message therefore performs a full working-tree hash on the Main process. Consider persisting/bounding the candidate read for read-only display paths (e.g. reuse while the Ledger revision and workspace mtimes are unchanged) so a polling UI does not repeatedly hash the entire repository.

reviewR53.overall_explanation: I inspected the full uncommitted TF-0672/A3 patch against the A3 requirements (harness/specs/tasks/autonomy-task-completion.md, harness/specs/guides/autonomous-project-system-plan.md) and the touched source, not just the last fixes. The core owner boundary holds: completion claims are refs-only, normalized/fenced before any append; Main independently re-resolves the workspace root and the runtime owner (readTaskLedgerAgentOwner), re-reads the actual candidate bytes and artifact files, re-reads the TaskLoop checkpoint refs via task_loop.completionEvidence, and fences the prefetched facts through A2 expectedRevision CAS fed by runtime-side completion_evidence_changed appends issued before config/checkpoint mutation under the existing journal lock. Replay is a read-only historical receipt (decisionScope operation-history) and the effective status is a separate read model, so failed attempts and later draft drift do not rewrite history. Generic non-user node mutations, id collision recasts, terminal manual done/dropped facts and caller-supplied completionDecision/completionReadback are all correctly blocked in projectTaskLedgerSnapshot and task-ledger-api, and vote/decision forging through appendEvents/updateNode is rejected. The exec foreground regression is genuinely fixed by intersecting the caller's allowBackground:false with the process policy, and the AWS/OS probe and Windows sharing retry are bounded and fail closed. I verified SHA256SUMS in the closure-audit fixture, the required test files, and the new gateway method registration/handler wiring. I did not find an exploitable security defect or a blocking correctness bug within the stated owner assumptions; the remaining items are a minor project-task progress regression, a dead/never-written verseshell receipt root (covered only by synthetic fixtures), and a repeated full-tree Git hash on polling paths. These are worth fixing but do not invalidate the admission boundary, so I mark the patch correct.

findings.title: Candidate scans have no cross-snapshot reuse
findings.reason: Ordinary reads now use async Git/fs and same-snapshot sharing, so Main is not synchronously held by the full filesystem scan. Source bytes can change without Ledgerrevision, directorymtime or filemtime/size changes (copy/restore timestamps). Cross-snapshot metadata reuse lacks an authoritative source mutation revision and would falsify current evidence. Added same-size/preserved-mtime byte-change regression and retained fresh read invariant. Further measured resource optimizations belong to existing resource/owner scopes and cannot silently trade freshness for a lower-cost display.
